'''Reinhold Aman''' (April 8, 1936 – March 2, 2019) was a [[chemical engineer]] and professor of German before achieving national and even international recognition as the publisher of ''[[Maledicta]]'', a [[scholarly journal]] dedicated to the study of offensive language, also known as [[maledictology]].

==Career==
Aman was born in [[Fürstenzell]] near [[Passau]], Bavaria.<ref name=DeG>{{cite journal |first=Tristan |last=Miller |title=Reinhold Aman, 1936–2019 |journal=Humor |volume=33 |issue=1 |year=2019 |pages=1–5 |doi=10.1515/humor-2019-0085 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=OracleOfOpprobium/> He studied chemical engineering in [[Augsburg]] and later worked as a chemical analyst and petroleum chemist in [[Frankfurt am Main|Frankfurt]], [[Munich]], and [[Montreal]] prior to working as a translator and clerk for the [[U.S. Army]] in Frankfurt. He moved to [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin|Milwaukee]] in 1959, initially working there as a metallurgist and analytical chemist.

Aman earned a [[bachelor's degree]] in German and secondary education at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] in 1965, and he completed a [[Ph.D.]] in German at the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]] in 1968 with a dissertation on ''"Der Kampf in Wolframs Parzival"'' ("Combat in  [[Wolfram von Eschenbach|Wolfram]]'s ''[[Parzival]]''").<ref name=DeG/> During his university years he taught German, French, Spanish, and English at various high schools, usually on a part-time basis. In his final year at Texas, he also served as a [[teaching assistant]] and [[teaching associate]].

Aman was hired in 1968 as an assistant professor of German at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]]<!-- (which he later dismissed as "Dungheap U"), --> where he taught undergraduate and graduate level courses in German, [[philology]], and [[medieval literature]] and in 1971 started ''Laugh and Learn'', a magazine of humorous material for second language learners. Denied [[Academic tenure|tenure]] in 1974, he held that he had been terminated out of "pure professional jealousy". He subsequently began publishing ''Maledicta'' from his home.<ref name=OracleOfOpprobium>{{cite journal |url=https://digitalcommons.butler.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=5921&context=wordways |title=The Oracle of Opprobium: Reinhold Aman, 1936–2019 |first=Tristan |last=Miller |journal=[[Word Ways]] |volume=53 |issue=2 |date=February 2020 |archive-date=April 17, 2021 |access-date=April 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417042031/https://digitalcommons.butler.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=5921&context=wordways |url-status=live }}</ref>

Apart from ''Maledicta'', Aman published a ''Bayrisch-Österreichisches Schimpfwörterbuch'' ("Bavarian-Austrian Curse Dictionary")<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sonic.net/maledicta/boes.html |title=Bilingual German/English announcement on Aman's website, with links |access-date=June 17, 2007 |archive-date=July 20, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090720041616/http://sonic.net/maledicta/boes.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> ({{ISBN|3-86520-095-8}}) and shorter monographs as well as various books, including ''[[Hillary Clinton]]'s Pen Pal: A Guide to Life and Lingo in Federal Prisons ''<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sonic.net/maledicta/penpal_contents.html |title=English-language announcement on Aman's website, with links |access-date=June 17, 2007 |archive-date=July 21, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090721203604/http://www.sonic.net/maledicta/penpal_contents.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> ({{ISBN|0-916500-14-4}}) (1996). At the time, Clinton was experiencing legal difficulties, and Aman claimed he wanted to make use of his recent term in federal prison to inform her about prison customs and [[argot]] so that she could avoid potentially lethal ''faux pas''.<ref name="OracleOfOpprobium" />

In 1983, Aman published a book of sex puns called ''How Do They Do It? A Collection of Wordplays Revealing the Sexual Proclivities of Man and Beast''.<ref name="OracleOfOpprobium" />

From the late 1990s until 2004, he was very active in online discussion fora.<ref name="OracleOfOpprobium" />

He appears in the 2005 documentary [[Fuck (2005 film)|''Fuck'']], in which he is described as "a cunning linguist".<ref>{{cite web |first=Amy M. |last=Cools |url=https://ordinaryphilosophy.com/tag/billy-connolly/ |title=Happy Birthday, H.P. Grice! |website=Ordinary Philosophy |date=March 13, 2019 |access-date=August 21, 2025 |archive-date=March 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230323151143/https://ordinaryphilosophy.com/tag/billy-connolly/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life, prison term, and final years==
In 1993, following a bitter divorce from his wife Shirley Aman, Aman was convicted on three counts of [[Threat#United States|mailing threatening communications]] and sentenced to 27 months in [[Federal Bureau of Prisons|federal prison]] for sending numerous Wisconsin lawyers and judges accounts of how he believed they should be shot, as well as for sending two postcards to his ex-wife with pasted-on headlines of news articles about women killed by their former husbands.<ref>{{cite news |first=David |last=Streitfeld |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1993/10/22/words/9a656ae4-6e8a-4f7c-9743-f6cafbd5ca2e/ |title=Words |newspaper=The Washington Post |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306064942/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1993/10/22/words/9a656ae4-6e8a-4f7c-9743-f6cafbd5ca2e/?utm_term=.6630712200e5 |archive-date=March 6, 2021 }}</ref> The sentence was reduced to 18 months on appeal;<ref name="OracleOfOpprobium"/> he served {{frac|15|1|2}} months at Santa Rita, [[Federal Correctional Institution, Terminal Island|Terminal Island]], [[Federal Correctional Institution, Lompoc|Lompoc]], and [[Federal Correctional Institution, Dublin|Dublin]] (now a Federal prison for women only). He was released in February 1995, whereupon he resumed the publication of ''Maledicta'', with the assistance of readers and friends plus the use of some of his retirement savings.<ref name=DeG/><ref name="OracleOfOpprobium" />

When ''Maledicta'' 13 appeared in 2005, Aman had become ill and was in debt. Evicted from his home in [[Santa Rosa, California]], he devoted much of his time to caring for stray and feral cats.<ref name="OracleOfOpprobium" /> He died on March 2, 2019, aged 82.<ref name=DeG/><ref name=OracleOfOpprobium/><ref>{{cite news |author=Koenen, Liesbeth |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2019/03/08/zelfs-hij-kreeg-kippenvel-van-de-allerergste-vloek-a3952602 |title=Zelfs hij kreeg kippenvel van de allerergste vloek |newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]] |date=March 8, 2019 |language=nl |archive-date=April 6, 2020 |access-date=March 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406220613/https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2019/03/08/zelfs-hij-kreeg-kippenvel-van-de-allerergste-vloek-a3952602 |url-status=live }}</ref>
